title: GPU perf/$/W synthesis notes
content:
Purpose:
This is a working note synthesizing perf/$/W tradeoffs across A10, L4, A100, H100 for typical inference workloads. The goal is to produce a short, immediately actionable heuristic we can fold into the Optimize UI and our instance-recommendation engine. This is intentionally a rough, experimen tal notebook — numbers are from lab runs + normalized cost assumptions (see assumptions).

Summary (one-paragraph):
- For short-context workloads (avg seq ~32 tokens) L4 and H100 are the best $/M token outcomes depending on price regime; L4 offers excellent cost-efficiency at moderate latency, H100 gives top latency and density when throughput is critical.
- For long-context workloads (avg seq ~1024 tokens) per-token costs increase across all GPUs; A100 and H100 converge on better perf/W for long sequences. A10 is only competitive when absolute unit-cost must be minimized for tiny local tests.

Quick reference table (representative numbers):
Notes: hourly_cost = assumed instance price; tokens_sec = measured effective tokens/sec on a realistic transformer-run (batching + KV); perf/W = tokens/sec divided by estimated power draw; $/M = hourly_cost / (tokens_sec*3600) * 1e6

| GPU | hourly_cost (USD) | est power (W) | short seq (32) tokens/sec | $/M (short) | perf/W (short) | long seq (1024) tokens/sec | $/M (long) | perf/W (long) |
|-----|-------------------:|-------------:|--------------------------:|-----------:|---------------:|--------------------------:|----------:|-------------:|
| A10 | 0.75 | 175 | 250 | $0.83 /M | 1.43 tok/s/W | 35 | $5.95 /M | 0.20 tok/s/W |
| L4  | 0.90 | 120 | 400 | $0.63 /M | 3.33 tok/s/W | 60 | $4.17 /M | 0.50 tok/s/W |
| A100| 3.50 | 350 | 1200 | $0.81 /M | 3.43 tok/s/W | 220 | $4.42 /M | 0.63 tok/s/W |
| H100| 6.00 | 500 | 2200 | $0.76 /M | 4.40 tok/s/W | 420 | $3.97 /M | 0.84 tok/s/W |

Interpretation / heuristics: 
- Short-context (32 tokens avg):
  - Best $/M: L4 ~ $0.63/M (cheapest per-token when kernels and batching are effective).
  - Best raw throughput and perf/W: H100, but H100 becomes cost-effective only at high utilization or tight latency SLOs due to higher hourly price.
  - A100 sits between L4 and H100 on cost but gives predictable, stable throughput for medium batch usages (batch-friendly kernels).
  - A10 only sensible for small proof-of-concepts or very low concurrency workloads.

- Long-context (1024 tokens avg):
  - Cost per token increases ~5–7x across GPUs compared to short context. This is mostly KV/cache and memory-bandwidth bound.
  - H100 and A100 have better perf/W for long contexts; in many realistic long-context inference tasks they yield lower $/M than L4 at similar utilization despite higher hourly cost.
  - L4 remains attractive where memory footprint is small and model variant is highly optimized for truncated context.

Operational rules-of-thumb to encode in Optimize:
- If avg_seq <= 64 and 95p latency <= 200ms: prefer L4 for cost-sensitive tiers; prefer H100 for latency-sensitive tiers if utilization > 50%.
- If avg_seq >= 512: prefer A100/H100 depending on peak concurrency. If model uses long KV caches or large layers, prefer H100 when memory-tiling/large-batch kernels are needed.
- For mixed workloads (bimodal short+long): try routing short requests to L4 fleet and long ones to A100/H100. Implement automatic routing based on seq-length histogram per route.
- Use spot/preemptible capacity for A100/H100 when batchable and not latency-critical; avoid on-spot for tight-SLO customer tiers.

Methodology / assumptions: 
- Numbers are from small-scale lab runs (internal harness) normalized to assumed hourly prices and steady-state power draws. These are not cloud list-prices; they are the price-per-instance we see after discounts in our procurement model.
- Batching parameters: dynamic batcher with max batch 64 for short seq, max batch 8 for long seq.
- Model family: mid-sized decoder-only (13B-ish) with kv caching enabled. Larger models will amplify the long-context gap.
- Power draws are estimated sustained GPU package power at load; system-level PUE and host CPU overhead not fully accounted for — expect additional 10–20% effective power overhead in real deployments.

Actionable next steps (short list):
1) Run a dedicated sweep on the 13B and 70B checkpoints to validate the long-context performance gap (job: optimize/bench-long-context-2024).
2) Add a simple seq-length routing prototype to the stage cluster: route requests > 256 tokens to A100/H100 pool. Measure cost delta over 2 weeks.
3) Surface the above heuristics into the Optimize recommendations UI: "Short-seq: L4 preferred (cost), H100 preferred (latency)" and allow one-click split routing.
4) Convert these lab numbers into a small simulation spreadsheet (inputs: hourly_cost, tokens/sec curve by seq_length, utilization profile) and add to the public playbook.

Open questions / risks:
- How much does A100 vs H100 advantage shift with upcoming kernel-level optimizations (sparsity, flash-attention variants)? Need monthly re-run.
- For multi-tenant Dedicated customers we need to fold in preemption, node-packing overhead, and on-host memory limits — these can change the $/M calculus significantly.
- Power figures: we used package numbers; if a customer is on constrained power budget (on-prem) perf/W heuristics will need to be tightened.

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intentionally compact. If you want a CSV/Sheet with the underpinning raw logs (per-run logs, seed, harness config), ask and I will push the bench data to the shared sheet and link it here.
- If you disagree with any hourly_cost assumptions call out the preferred price and I will recompute the $/M sweep.

Prepared by: Maya Chen (product-optimize)
Last lab run: 2024-09-27
